players.product: CMP diamond pad conditioners and reclaimed wafers

quarterly_data.signal: Kinik investor deck (Macquarie Asia Unbound Conference): 1Q26 consolidated revenue NT$2,293,229 thousand (NTD 2.29B), up 5.6% QoQ and 29.4% YoY; gross margin 35.0% (+0.8 ppt QoQ; 30.9% in 1Q25); operating margin 19.4%; net income to shareholders of the parent NT$436,359 thousand (+52.7% YoY); EPS NTD 2.94. The company says revenue and gross margin growth were mainly driven by QoQ growth across all three business units.
quarterly_data.figure: 1Q26 revenue NTD 2.29B (+5.6% QoQ, +29.4% YoY); gross margin 35.0%; operating margin 19.4%; EPS NTD 2.94

quarterly_data.signal: 1Q26 by business unit: DBU (CMP diamond disk) revenue NT$717,188 thousand (31% of sales, +5.0% QoQ, +27.7% YoY), supported by higher CMP diamond disk shipments for 2nm processes and U.S. IDM customers; SBU (test/reclaim wafer) NT$1,032,486 thousand (45%, +6.3% QoQ, +13.6% YoY), driven by full utilization of 330K/month 12-inch capacity and increased shipments of high-end reclaim wafers; 12-inch reclaim wafer sales increased 12.8%. For one specific (unnamed) customer, the revenue ratio from its advanced technologies (sub-5nm) products and advanced packaging rose 58%, and 16nm and 2nm diamond disk shipments surged 39% and 20%.
quarterly_data.figure: DBU NT$717,188 thousand (+5.0% QoQ, +27.7% YoY); SBU NT$1,032,486 thousand (+6.3% QoQ); 12-inch capacity 330K/month fully utilized

quarterly_data.signal: Kinik 2025 overview (deck): 2025 revenue NTD 8,149M, EPS 9.28; 2025 sales ratio: grinding wheel (ABU and subsidiaries) 23%, CMP diamond disk (DBU) 31%, reclaim and test Si wafer (SBU) 46%. In 2025, revenue from semiconductor industries was ~6.6 billion (80% of total Kinik revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue NTD 8,149M; semiconductor ~6.6 billion (80% of total)

quarterly_data.signal: Kinik 2026 outlook (deck): demand for diamond disks used in advanced processes and advanced packaging is expected to increase quarter by quarter; market share and shipments with U.S. IDM customers are expected to continue ramping up quarterly. All newly added 12-inch wafer capacity will be dedicated to high-end reclaimed wafers for advanced node customers, optimizing the mix toward high-end applications to boost revenue and gross margin.

Kinik capacity (deck): CMP diamond disk monthly capacity reached 50K units in 1Q26 and will expand to over 60K units from 3Q26; 12-inch reclaim/test wafer capacity is fully loaded and was increased by 30K wafers/month to 360K starting 2Q, expanding further to 400K wafers/month from 3Q.
